messages:
jordan-cust: Hi team — since yesterday our Redwood API calls from our on-prem app are getting routed to eu-west-1. Latency spiked from ~30ms to ~350ms and a few auth tokens started failing (403). We didn't change region config. Any ideas?
ben-support: Sorry you're hitting that, jordan. Can you paste a curl -v response (headers) and one server-side request log showing the client IP/redwood region header if available?
jordan-cust: pasted curl -v output below (IP and host redacted):
---curl start---
*   Trying 34.200.11.12...
* Connected to api.redwood.example (34.200.11.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
< content-type: application/json
< content-length: 512
---curl end---
Also our app logs show source public IP 51.15.23.67 (company egress). Geo lookup puts that in Paris.
ben-support: Thanks. Seeing x-redwood-region: eu-west-1 is the clue — our smart routing picks region based on perceived client location (source IP) when customers use default routing. Looks like your egress IP geolocates to EU.
sam-infra: Quick diagnostic checklist: 1) Is your on-prem egress going through a corporate proxy in EU? 2) Are you SNATting to a single egress IP that resolves to EU? 3) Any transit peering that hairpins traffic through EU?
jordan-cust: We do have a transparent proxy that peers to our EU office for outbound traffic (we thought it was just for updates). We didn't think it would affect region selection.
alek-network: That will do it — SNAT/central proxy hides original client location. Two options: preserve a US egress IP (egress NAT in US region) or configure your proxy to add an explicit region hint header.
ben-support: For a short-term workaround you can set an explicit region hint header in your requests: X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: us-east-1 (we can honor that header for accounts with private deployments). If you want ops to enable it on your account we can toggle it on our side for a day while you adjust network.
jordan-cust: Appreciate that. Can you confirm if the header is supported for Private/VPC endpoints?
ben-support: Yes — for Private customers we accept X-Redwood-Prefer-Region on authenticated requests. We'll need your account id to scope the override.
alek-network: Long term: avoid SNAT to EU. If you're on AWS, add a NAT Gateway/egress IP in us-east-1 and route outbound to it, or use a regional egress edge. If using corporate proxy, enable passing original client IP via X-Forwarded-For and ensure it does not SNAT to EU address space.
jordan-cust: Repro steps we'll run: 1) curl -v against private endpoint and confirm x-redwood-region 2) run curl with X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: us-east-1 and verify 3) traceroute to check path 4) check proxy NAT rules.
sam-infra: Helpful commands:
- curl -v -H "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: us-east-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/meta -D -
- curl -sS https://ipinfo.io/ip (from your app host)
- sudo iptables -t nat -L -n | grep MASQUERADE
If your iptables shows MASQUERADE for outbound, that'll SNAT to the proxy/gateway IP.
jordan-cust: Ran the tests — with header we get x-redwood-region: us-east-1 and latency back to 25ms. iptables shows MASQUERADE on the proxy host.
ben-support: Great narrow-down. Next steps we suggest: 1) We can enable account-scoped region hint for 48h so apps don't break. Please DM account id. 2) Your network team should change NAT so egress IP is in us-east-1 or remove SNAT at proxy. 3) We can add a synthetic check on your account to alert if detected-source-region != configured-region.
jordan-cust: I'll DM account id now and loop in network team. Thanks all.
deploy-bot: Incident note: temporary routing override applied to acct-724 for 48h (actioned by ben-support) :white_check_mark:
ben-support: Leaving this thread open — ping here once network change is rolled out and we'll remove the override. :thumbsup:
